checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001/tb-002/tb-003: Does bytes_to_bls_field reject integers >= BLS_MODULUS?

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit blob data via type-3 transactions or send crafted cells via P2P gossip. Blob bytes are deserialized into field elements via bytes_to_bls_field in cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001). If the range check is missing, modular reduction silently corrupts data.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify the bytes_to_bls_field function in the KZG implementation (cell_to_coset_evals in SG-001). 2. Verify the function performs explicit range checking: value < BLS_MODULUS MUST be enforced before any field operations. 3. Test with boundary values: (a) BLS_MODULUS - 1 (should succeed), (b) BLS_MODULUS (should fail), (c) BLS_MODULUS + 1 (should fail), (d) 2^256 - 1 (should fail). 4. Verify the rejection is a hard error, not a silent modular reduction. 5. Check all code paths that call bytes_to_bls_field: transaction processing, P2P cell reception, blob reconstruction. 6. Verify the BLS_MODULUS constant is correctly defined (52435875175126190479447740508185965837690552500527637822603658699938581184513). 7. Test with crafted blob data where bytes 0-31 represent a value >= BLS_MODULUS. 8. Verify error handling propagates correctly to reject the entire blob/cell, not just the field element.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-1, Trust Boundaries: tb-001, tb-002, tb-003. This is the primary boundary check. Silent modular reduction instead of rejection would allow invalid field elements to corrupt the polynomial commitment pipeline.

checklist_with_code.code_excerpt: // NOT_FOUND: bytes_to_bls_field / cell_to_coset_evals are EIP-7594 spec functions for cell KZG processing (PeerDAS). These are consensus-layer functions not implemented in reth. The c_kzg external library used by reth handles blob KZG internally without exposing bytes_to_bls_field.

checklist_item.title: Falsification Test: Can out-of-range blob bytes produce cells that pass verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit blob data via type-3 transactions or send crafted cells via P2P gossip. Blob bytes are deserialized into field elements via bytes_to_bls_field in cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001). If the range check is missing, modular reduction silently corrupts data.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. SETUP: Prepare a valid blob with all field elements < BLS_MODULUS. Compute its KZG commitment and cells with proofs. 2. ATTACK CONSTRUCTION: (a) Take a valid blob, (b) Replace one or more 32-byte chunks with values >= BLS_MODULUS, (c) Specifically test: BLS_MODULUS, BLS_MODULUS + 1, 2^256 - 1, and values just above BLS_MODULUS. 3. INJECTION: Submit the modified blob via type-3 transaction OR send crafted cells via P2P gossip. 4. OBSERVATION: Track whether bytes_to_bls_field applies modular reduction (silent corruption) or rejects. 5. EXPECTED RESULT: The system should reject the blob/cells at entry point. bytes_to_bls_field should return an error. 6. FALSIFICATION SUCCESS (BUG FOUND) IF: (a) bytes_to_bls_field applies modular reduction silently (value % BLS_MODULUS), (b) The resulting cells pass verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch, (c) The corrupted data propagates to other nodes, (d) Validators attest to blocks with this corrupted data. 7. PoC REQUIREMENTS per bug bounty notes: Demonstrate an out-of-range blob byte sequence that produces a cell passing verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch but committing to incorrect data.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-1, Bug Bounty Notes: 'Requires PoC demonstrating that an out-of-range blob byte sequence produces a cell that passes verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch but commits to incorrect data.'

checklist_item.title: Verify Implementation Consistency: Do all bytes_to_bls_field implementations use consistent range checking?

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit blob data via type-3 transactions or send crafted cells via P2P gossip. Blob bytes are deserialized into field elements via bytes_to_bls_field in cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001). If the range check is missing, modular reduction silently corrupts data.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify all implementations of bytes_to_bls_field across the codebase (may be in different modules or libraries). 2. Verify each implementation checks value < BLS_MODULUS BEFORE any field operations. 3. Compare implementations: (a) Do they all use the same BLS_MODULUS constant? (b) Do they all return errors (not silent reduction)? (c) Do they all check the same byte ordering (big-endian vs little-endian)? 4. Check for alternative field element construction paths that might bypass the standard bytes_to_bls_field. 5. Verify library dependencies (e.g., BLST, Arkworks) implement range checking correctly. 6. checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Are all commitment_indices validated to be within bounds of the deduplicated commitments array before array access?

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) in the codebase. 2. Identify where commitment_indices array is processed and used to index into the deduplicated commitments array. 3. Verify explicit bounds checking: for each index k, confirm commitment_indices[k] < len(commitments) is validated BEFORE array access. 4. Check if bounds checking uses signed vs unsigned comparison (potential integer underflow). 5. Craft malicious P2P message with commitment_indices containing values >= len(commitments). 6. Submit via P2P gossip and verify: a) Request is rejected with appropriate error, OR b) Node crashes (vulnerability confirmed). 7. Test edge cases: commitment_indices[k] == len(commitments) (off-by-one), commitment_indices[k] == MAX_UINT (overflow), empty commitments array with non-empty indices. 8. Verify memory safety: if language has unchecked array access, confirm explicit bounds checking exists.
